Hi Sophie — quick note to remove ambiguity.

Jordan’s initial note used "PT." Because US daylight savings begins on Sunday, March 8 this year, times on March 10 should be interpreted as Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), not PST. So:

- 10:00 AM PT (on Mar 10) = 10:00 AM PDT = 17:00 UTC = 18:00 CET (Central European Time, currently UTC+1) = 22:30 IST (UTC+5:30)
- 11:30 AM PDT = 18:30 UTC = 19:30 CET = 00:00 IST (next day)
- 2:00 PM PDT = 21:00 UTC = 22:00 CET = 03:30 IST (next day)

Because CET will not switch to CEST until March 29, CET is still UTC+1 on March 10.

If BrightRetail wants to avoid after-10pm IST times for the Mumbai stakeholder, Option A (10:00 AM PDT) is the best of those three — it lands at 22:30 IST, which is late but still doable once in a while. If THAT is too late, we can instead offer something earlier for PDT (e.g., 8:30 AM PDT = 15:30 UTC = 16:30 CET = 21:00 IST).

I’ll let Jordan/Dylan re-propose with final time options and I can add the UTC offsets in the calendar invite.

Thanks —
Marissa
